analysis.title: The Credit Line: From Shell to Compute: An Update on AI Project Finance
key_insights: Year-to-date AI project finance issuance is $80B across IG and HY datacenter bonds, plus $22B of non-syndicated datacenter construction financing and $48B of chip (compute) financing. Earlier this year GS tracked a $76B datacenter bond market.
GS raises its 2027 global AI project finance issuance forecast to $545B ($225B shells, $320B compute), from a prior $300B and more than double the earlier estimate.

Risks to the forecast are two-sided. Upside: rising capex and saturation in higher-rated corporate credit push more supply into structured formats at wider spreads. Downside: construction delays, tighter financing economics and moratoria on new builds.

Tighter economics already slowed issuance in 4Q2026 while growing the backlog. GS economists view the moratoria as conditional, focused on new builds and likely to fade, but sustained curtailment could weigh on 2027 financing.

Chip financings use bankruptcy-remote SPVs, structured as equipment leases or compute service contracts. Investors underwrite contract, project and counterparty risk rather than pure corporate credit risk.
GS favors chip equipment leases and service contracts with narrow SLAs. Contracts with wide SLA perimeters, where service deficiencies haircut revenue, are least favorable.

Credit investors should avoid assuming GPU obsolescence risk where possible. Protections in practice are amortizing debt and lease terms that match or exceed debt tenor. Traditional first-lien financing is not equipped to underwrite fast-depreciating assets at this size.

Most GPU financings so far are delayed-draw term loans. GS expects larger deals to need cross-market participation or IG market access, and expects draw periods to shorten as shells come online, shifting issuers from ticking fees toward bond structures.

Chip suppliers guarantee some or all of the debt through residual value guarantees, typically close to outstanding principal and remaining interest. This exposes chipmaker ratings to a left-tail scenario, and rating agencies have flagged compounding exposure across deals.

Chipmaker CDS trades at a growing premium to cash bonds because credit support has been extended without matching bond issuance. Hyperscalers issued over $295B globally this year and are nearly $450B of the USD IG index, while chipmakers in the sample issued under $35B with $94B of index-eligible notional. GS expects the chipmaker CDS-cash premium to keep rising.

Chip financing leases of five years or shorter concentrate supply in the belly of the curve. This creates technical flattening pressure on AI-related curves, but growing guarantee obligations should put a floor under long-end spreads and limit a rally in longer-tenor AI debt.

Bonds with 3-7 year maturities were 60% of non-financial issuer count and 40% of non-financial supply value in USD IG over the past two years, so more front-end AI issuance at wider spreads could weigh on non-AI credit.

GS expects the AI vs non-AI bifurcation to persist. Meaningful spillover needs IG index eligibility of structured financings, investor comfort with structured lease financing, and willingness to stretch sector concentration limits for carry.

HY datacenter bonds are held at an average -0.07% active weight in mutual funds and ETFs (average portfolio weight 0.08% vs benchmark 0.15%). Aggregate-type mandates and insurers are the main IG datacenter bond holders.

Higher base rates and a higher AI risk premium have lifted yields on new datacenter bonds, while spreads have been more mixed. Rates are a drag on issuance through rent pricing and deal economics, and GS expects more equity, lower LTCs or tighter structures if tenants resist higher rents.

GS recommends a patient, selective approach that underwrites project specifics rather than macro beta, which can drive spreads wider but not meaningfully tighter. It also expects evidence of AI monetization to matter more to credit investors over the next few quarters.

sector_views.sector: AI datacenter and compute project finance
sector_views.rationale: Forecast supply surges to $545B in 2027, but GS recommends a patient, selective approach underwriting project specifics, with spreads more likely to go wider than tighter on macro beta.
Residual value guarantees add left-tail exposure, and the CDS-cash premium is expected to keep rising as the credit footprint outgrows the bond footprint.

risk_factors: Construction delays or moratoria on new datacenter builds, perceived or actual, could slow 2027 financing.
Tighter financing economics from higher rates and a higher AI risk premium.
Residual value guarantee exposure compounding across chip deals, which rating agencies have flagged.
Supply saturation and issuer and thematic concentration in IG credit.
Front-end AI issuance at wider spreads could weigh on non-AI corporate spreads given 60% of non-financial issuers sit at 3-7 year tenors.
Uncertainty about monetization of AI investment and sentiment swings.
Complexity premium and loose call protection limit broad HY investor overweights.
Compute financing forecast is sensitive to the financed-share assumption.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows realized 2025 and 2026 AI-related project finance issuance and the 2027 estimate of $545B, split into $225B datacenter and $320B chip/compute.
Exhibit 7 shows HY datacenter bond portfolio weight versus benchmark weight, with an average active weight of -0.07%.
Exhibit 10 shows the percentage-point change in yield-on-cost needed to hold a given DSCR for coupons of 7.0% to 10.5%, with a base case of 8% coupon and 1.2 DSCR at zero change.
vol_and_positioning: HY datacenter bonds are held at -0.07% average active weight in mutual funds and ETFs, so positioning is light.
Chipmaker CDS premium over representative cash bond spreads is wider than hyperscalers' and GS expects it to keep rising.
Hyperscaler cash bonds have been pushed wider by heavy issuance and saturation, partly offsetting their CDS premium.
Aggregate-mandate funds and insurers are the main holders of IG datacenter bonds, which are off the BBG US Aggregate and US Corporate indices.

tension_points.bull_case: Rising capex and saturation in corporate credit push more supply into structured formats, lifting 2027 issuance to $545B, with 2027 compute financing of $320B.
tension_points.bear_case: Construction delays, tighter financing economics and potential moratoria on new builds could slow the buildout and 2027 financing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More sustained or aggressive curtailment of construction, such as moratoria on new builds, would weigh on 2027 financing.

tension_points.bull_case: Chip financing concentrated in the belly of the curve creates technical flattening pressure on AI-related curves.
tension_points.bear_case: Growing residual value guarantee obligations and a higher credit risk premium put a floor under long-end spreads and limit a rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed volatility in the outlook for AI spending would bring the fundamental overhang into focus.

tension_points.bull_case: Chip financing carry could attract investors and compete with front-end non-AI debt, repricing credit more broadly.
tension_points.bear_case: Bifurcation persists because structured financings are off IG index, investors lack comfort with the structures, and sector concentration limits bind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: IG index eligibility of structured financings together with investor comfort with structures and sector concentration.
